amendment: Transport only. The Anthropic Messages API path was replaced by a company-broker-authenticated isolated one-shot Claude Code subprocess, because the Messages API required separately billed credentials this project does not have. No research semantics changed: the prompt template, candidate derivation, validation gates, retry budgets and SILENCE policy are byte-identical to the original freeze, which is why spec_version is still condition-c-v1. The original tag remains in place and config/condition_c_model_v1.json was superseded rather than edited; its hash below is the same value the original manifest recorded.
note: Condition C is frozen BEFORE the holdout it will be scored on exists. It has never been run on heldout-v3, on any scenario in it, or on any state derived from one. Its confirmatory evaluation uses a new holdout generated only after this freeze.

model_transport_invocation.note: The exact frozen command line. Every isolation flag Condition C relies on is in this file; check_condition_c_freeze.py cross-checks it against the config's transport block.

superseded_model_configuration.note: The Messages API config of the original freeze. Unused by the current transport and retained unedited. This hash is identical to the one tagged condition-c-pre-v4-freeze, which is the evidence that the amendment superseded it rather than rewriting it.

transport_tests.note: Offline. Runs the real wrapper against a fake claude binary that records argv, environment, cwd and stdin.

isolation_canary.note: Live. Asks the model what it can see, with freshly minted random bait planted where the CLI would look. Includes a negative control that must leak.

live_smoke.note: Live, one invented scenario, scores nothing and tunes nothing. Not part of the default battery.

evaluation_protocol.note: Append-only pin, not a whole-file pin. The protocol is a living document that must keep growing: the heldout-v4 evaluation plan was appended as §12 after this freeze, and later phases will append more. The hash above covers the first 38198 bytes, which are byte-for-byte the protocol as it stood at condition-c-pre-v4-freeze-v2 (§1 through §11, ending with the heldout-v3 closure). A single edited or deleted byte before that offset fails this check; anything appended after it does not. Condition C reads no protocol text at run time, so appending to it cannot change what C does.

freeze_checker.note: Changed once since condition-c-pre-v4-freeze-v2, at the heldout-v4 specification freeze, in exactly one function: check_hashes now honours an optional frozen_prefix_bytes key. Entries without that key are verified byte-for-byte as before, so every hash that mattered to Condition C is checked exactly as it was. The one entry that uses it, evaluation_protocol, is deliberately a weaker claim than a whole-file hash -- a prefix rather than the file -- because the protocol must keep growing; in exchange it also fails on truncation, which a whole-file mismatch could not distinguish from an ordinary edit. The previous hash is recorded above and the version it names is recoverable from the tag, so this amendment is legible without git and cannot be mistaken for a silent weakening.

unchanged_since_heldout_v3_evaluation.note: These are the frozen artifacts of the CLOSED heldout-v3 experiment. Neither this freeze nor the transport amendment touched them. The hashes below are the same values check_heldout_v3_evaluation_integrity.py verifies.

model_configuration.sampling_note: The Claude Code CLI exposes no temperature, top_p, top_k, max_tokens or seed flag. Every one of these is null because nothing is sent, not because a default was chosen. Condition C is LESS controllable under this transport than it was under the Messages API, where temperature 0 was available. That is a real cost of the amendment and is recorded rather than smoothed over.
model_configuration.determinism_note: No sampling parameter can be set and no seed exists, so repeated runs on identical input may differ. Condition C is NOT a deterministic condition; Conditions A and B are. Every raw response is logged verbatim so a diverging rerun is visible.

transport.authentication: company-managed Claude Code broker (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN + loopback ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL)
transport.isolation_principle: Authentication must not imply semantic context inheritance. The subprocess inherits the broker credential and nothing else.
model_sees: the frozen Condition C system/task prompt
the hard-eligible candidate hints for that scenario
transport.known_injected_context: Under --print the CLI injects a system reminder stating the current date. It is not suppressible from the command line, carries no repository, benchmark or conversation content, and no prompt in this protocol refers to a date. Recorded rather than omitted.
transport.isolation_verified_behaviourally: At its root command this CLI silently tolerates unknown options, so flag acceptance is not evidence of isolation. The live canary asks the model what it can see, with bait planted; the offline transport suite captures what the child process actually received.
